 Stewart challenges Glens to turn improvement into consistency
 Fri 6 Nov 2026, 18:00
 Share
 Jordan Stewart believes Glentoran’s recent improvement must be the starting point for more as the Glens prepare to visit Carrick Rangers on Saturday.
 The forward has welcomed the progress of the past six weeks but insists the quality within the squad demands a sustained level of performance.
 Having returned to the starting line-up with a goal at Coleraine following absences through suspension and a minor injury, Stewart is keen to help the Glens recover ground lost earlier in the campaign.
 “We’ve obviously got a really good squad here. There’s a lot of talent in the group,” he said.
 “We were massively underachieving, selling ourselves short at the start of the season. 
 “We’ve definitely picked up in probably the last six weeks. But it’s not really enough. We need to keep going. We need to keep trying to perform.” 
 Saturday’s Irish Premiership fixture at Taylor’s Avenue (kick-off: 3pm) provides the next opportunity to meet that challenge.
 For Stewart, the depth of the squad gives Glentoran reason for confidence, while the points dropped earlier in the season provide motivation to maintain their progress.
 “I think results have been good,” he continued.
 “We’ve left a lot of points behind at the start of the season. But we’ve a lot of games now left to end the season. Hopefully we can make them back up.” 
 Stewart’s return to the side comes as the players adjust to Duncan Ferguson’s demands on the training pitch.
 The 31-year-old has enjoyed the intensity of the sessions and the process of adapting to a new manager, with both sides learning more about one another.
 “He’s been getting to know the group. We’ve been getting to know him,” Stewart explained.
 “There’s a lot of intensity to the training.” 
 While acknowledging that the demands take some getting used to, his assessment of the work has been positive.
 “I’ve thoroughly enjoyed it so far,” he added.
 Stewart will hope to build on his involvement at The Showgrounds, where his late header secured a point in Ferguson’s first game in charge.
 “It was good to be back in the team last week,” he said.
 The focus now turns to making another contribution at Carrick, with the travelling Glentoran support providing an added incentive.
 “It’s a great following. The support means a lot,” Stewart said.
 “Hopefully we send them home with three points and something to cheer about come Saturday evening.”
